questions.stem: Per this page, what happens when a subclass overrides a `synchronized` method of its parent and leaves out the keyword?

options.text: The override runs without holding the monitor, so the parent's thread safety is quietly lost
options.says: The page says the subclass method then runs without holding the monitor, silently breaking the parent's thread safety.

options.text: The override takes on the parent's modifier, so it still runs while holding the monitor
options.says: The page says that without the keyword the subclass method runs without holding the monitor.

options.text: The compiler rejects the override, since it must repeat every modifier the parent used
options.says: The page's ExtendedCounter example overrides increment() without the keyword; it compiles and breaks thread safety.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

questions.stem: Per this page, why implement `Runnable` for a worker's logic rather than extend `Thread`?

options.text: It separates what the task does from how it runs, and frees the superclass slot
options.says: The page says extending Thread uses up the single inheritance slot and conflates what to do with how to run it.

options.text: It binds the task to platform threads, so it cannot move to a virtual thread
options.says: The page's Runnable DataProcessor 'Can run on platform threads, virtual threads, or single-threaded executor'.

options.text: It gives the task setPriority and setDaemon, which the task code relies on
options.says: The page says Thread is a heavy class with many methods (setPriority, setDaemon, etc.) that are irrelevant to the task logic.
